message.reasoning: Okay, so I need to figure out whether deleting my step brother's profile on my Nintendo Switch is morally acceptable. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I had to watch my step brother for a week while my dad and his mom were on a trip. I brought my Switch because I wanted something to do during my long commute to school. My step brother really liked playing on it, so I created a new profile for him to keep his games separate from mine. That way, he could play without messing up my saves. When I got back to school, I got annoyed because every time I started a game or went to the eShop, I had to click on my profile. It was a small inconvenience, but it annoyed me enough that I decided to delete his profile. I thought it wasn't a big deal because I usually don't bring my Switch over when I visit. Now, during Thanksgiving, my step brother found out his Zelda save was gone and started crying. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because he knew my step brother was enjoying playing on it. I didn't think it was a big deal, but now I'm feeling bad because it affected him emotionally. So, is deleting his profile morally acceptable? Let's break it down. On one hand, the Switch is my property, and I have the right to manage who uses it and how. Creating a profile for him was a considerate gesture to prevent any issues with my games. However, deleting his profile without discussing it with him or considering his feelings might be where the problem lies. I should think about the impact of my action. My step brother was emotionally affected, which shows that the profile meant something to him. Even though I didn't think it was a big deal, it clearly was for him. That lack of consideration for his feelings could be seen as mean or unfair. Additionally, my dad's reaction indicates that he believes it was mean, which adds another layer to the situation. It's important to respect family dynamics and consider how actions affect others, especially when it comes to shared or borrowed items. In conclusion, while I had the right to manage my Switch, the way I handled the situation by deleting the profile without communication and consideration for my step brother's feelings makes the action morally unacceptable.
